summary.text: After the member passes away, apply for a grant of letters of administration, then approach the Public Trustee’s Office.

details.heading: Where the CPF savings go
details.body: Upon the member’s passing, CPF savings are transferred to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution to family members under intestacy laws or inheritance laws for Muslims.

steps.name: Apply for a grant
steps.text: If the member passed away without making a CPF nomination, apply for a grant of letters of administration.

steps.name: Approach the PTO
steps.text: After you apply for the grant, approach the Public Trustee’s Office to proceed with the distribution.

about.text: The Public Trustee’s Office charges an administrative fee for this service.

example_phrasings: What happens to CPF without a nomination?

sources.page_title: If the deceased passed on without a will and did not make a CPF nomination. Will CPF contact the next-of-kin directly or do we need to appoint an administrator ourselves?

quotes.text: The next-of-kin would have to apply for a grant of letters of administration and approach PTO to proceed with the distribution.
PTO will charge an administrative fee for this service.

If a member did not make a CPF nomination, upon his/her passing, his/her CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution to family members under intestacy laws or inheritance laws (for Muslims).
